corrected_value.authors: Giovannelli F., Borgheresi A., Balestrieri F., Zaccara G., Viggiano M. P., Cincotta M., et al.
corrected_value.title: Modulation of interhemispheric inhibition by volitional motor activity: an ipsilateral silent period study.

decisions.quote: The iSP paradigm was found to be inadequate for the aim, as the iSP was not modulated by hand contraction. In fact, during the iSP paradigm we manipulated the activity of the contralateral hand, expecting to induce a stronger interhemispheric inhibition in the Contracted compared to the Relaxed condition (Giovannelli et al., 2009 ), which we did not observe. The null result on iSP modulation was surprising, considering the consistent effects reported previously throughout several manipulations of contralateral hand activity (Giovannelli et al., 2009 ).
decisions.reason: In the source paper (Zazio et al., 2022), the authors manipulate contralateral hand activity (Contracted vs. Relaxed) during the ipsilateral silent period (iSP) paradigm specifically to reproduce the interhemispheric inhibition modulation reported by Giovannelli et al. (2009, 10.1113/jphysiol.2009.175885), test Contracted vs. Relaxed in the Results (t(19) = -1.67, p = 0.94; Bayesian t-test BF01 = 5.95), and explicitly state in the Discussion (line 1) that they expected 'to induce a stronger interhemispheric inhibition in the Contracted compared to the Relaxed condition (Giovannelli et al., 2009 ), which we did not observe.' The only shipped row for this work (input_row_index 855) is Bortoletto et al. (2021, 10.1016/j.brs.2021.02.002), which concerns early latency TMS-EEG P25 connectivity rather than iSP modulation by contralateral hand contraction. Thus, Giovannelli et al. (2009) is a genuinely absent replication-original pair.
